title: HIVE: A High-Priority Victim Cache for Accelerating GPU Memory Accesses
problem: GPU memory hierarchies suffer from high latency when victim caches are accessed as secondary L1D miss handlers, particularly for memory-intensive workloads.
motivation: CPU-inspired victim cache designs are suboptimal for GPUs; accessing both L1D and its victim cache incurs excessive latency, degrading performance for certain application classes.
method: HIVE redesigns the victim cache to handle memory requests before L1D access. High-priority victim cache provides direct low-latency memory request handling, bypassing the L1D cache for certain access patterns. Architectural modification prioritizes victim cache lookups for the most latency-critical requests.
key_novelty: Victim cache hierarchy inversion: handling requests at victim cache level before L1D to reduce critical path latency.
contributions: High-priority victim cache design with early memory request interception
77.1% average performance improvement over baseline GPU
21.7% improvement over prior state-of-the-art GPU cache architecture
limitations: Workload scope and specific GPU architecture not detailed; applicability to different GPU families unclear.
primary_theme: Victim cache prioritization for GPU memory latency
